subject: Vendor activation — consolidate remit lanes, propose hybrid net-tier & early-pay opt-in

To: sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Cardinal Systems AP <ap@cardinalsys.com>
Date: 2026-06-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Vendor onboarding — invoice lanes & payment terms

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the onboarding window last week. We're working through vendor setup items on our end and wanted to align on a couple of things before we complete your AP form:

- Our standard is Net 60. For cashflow reasons we'd like to understand if Redwood can accept Net 30 for the one-time implementation invoice (SOW work) while keeping Net 60 for the monthly usage invoices.
- We're also interested in an early-pay option — if Redwood offers a discount for accelerated payment, please share terms (rate, enrollment lead time).
- How should POs be sent to you? Do you prefer AP email, portal upload, or a PO number in the invoice header?

I've attached our completed vendor form (Cardinal_AP_Form_v2.pdf). Can you confirm the point of contact and next steps to activate the correct remit lanes in your system?

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Dana
Dana Miller
Finance Manager, Cardinal Systems

Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding — invoice lanes & payment terms

Hi Dana — thanks for the form and the clear asks. Quick answers and proposed next steps: 

1) Hybrid net-tier: We can support Net 30 for any one-time implementation / SOW line items and Net 60 for recurring usage charges. We'll need the invoice to clearly label line items and include the PO number where required.

2) Early-pay program: We offer an optional early-pay enrollment (pilot) that gives a 1.0% discount for invoices paid within 10 days. Enrollment typically takes ~7 business days after the vendor record is active. If you want a larger discount for guaranteed accelerated remit (e.g., 2% for 5-day payment), that's something we can evaluate but it requires procurement approval.

3) PO & remit lanes: Preferred flow is PO number on invoice + electronic routing to ap@redwoodinference.com. We also support vendor portal uploads for high-volume suppliers. If Cardinal will send POs from a shared system, paste the PO email alias in the vendor form so we can whitelist it.

Action items from Redwood (me / procurement):
- Karthik will validate which ledger/GL the onboarding fees should hit and confirm whether the implementation SOW can be treated as Net 30.
- Marissa will provision the vendor record and set remit lanes (ap@redwoodinference.com) once we receive the signed form and W-9 if applicable.

Can you confirm the preferred remit email address for PO receipts and whether Cardinal is OK with the 1.0% early-pay pilot for Net 30 invoices? If yes, we'll kick off activation and share a DocuSign link for the early-pay addendum.

Thanks — Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Strategic Ops, Redwood Inference

Looping in procurement details / internal checklist:

- Confirmed: we can treat onboarding SOWs as Net 30 with the caveat that invoices must be clearly scoped and tied to an approved PO. No mixed-line ambiguity (procurement needs the PO reference).
- AP routing: ap@redwoodinference.com is the canonical inbox. If Cardinal requires PO upload to their portal, they should cc that inbox as well so we capture the invoice.
- Discount mechanics: the 1.0% early-pay (10-day) is acceptable for a pilot. For any below-10-day offers we need to run a cost/benefit with finance — will need gross margin impact and expected volume estimate.

Marissa — pls add Cardinal Systems as follows: remit lane = ap@redwoodinference.com; payment terms map = {implementation: NET30, recurring: NET60}; attach the vendor form and request W-9. Also tag this as an early-pay pilot candidate and set a 45-day activation SLA.

Karthik
